I've been working this land for forty years. My hands know this soil, and I know what grows well here in Quzhou. The well gives me water when the rains fail, and that matters more than anything else.

I'm getting older and I'm alone this year, so I have to be practical. Cotton takes too much picking by hand — I'll keep a small patch because I know it and the seeds are already paid for, but I won't push myself. Wheat I always plant, that's food and income. Chili is my main thing — I've grown it for years, I know how to tend it, and the buyers come to me. Watermelon does well here with irrigation, and garlic I can do alongside wheat since the timing fits. Fourteen mu between five crops — that's what I know, that's what I'll do.

I'll rotate the chili away from where I had it last year to keep the soil from souring. Wheat goes in first in October after I finish the garlic planting. Come spring I put in watermelon. Chili and cotton go in when it warms up in May.

I use the fertilizer amounts I learned from my neighbors and from what I've seen work — probably more nitrogen than officials say but that's how we get yield around here. I irrigate from the well when I see the soil drying out or when the plants show stress.
